correctness.rationale: Exact two-point counting-measure example H=H0=C^2, k=diag(1,0), f(1)=g(1)=e1 and f(2)=g(2)=e2 is Parseval/Bessel. For every h=(a,b), both 2020 journal scalar tests equal |a|^2=||kh||^2 while T_fT_g*=I != k (witness e2). Direct independent SymPy matrix arithmetic verified k*(I-k)=0 and e2 contradiction. In arbitrary COMPLEX Hilbert spaces with bounded Bessel maps, polarization of <(M-k)h,kh>=0 gives k*(M-k)=0, equivalent to P_{closure R(k)} M=k; the second test analogously gives k(N-k*)=0. In particular R(M) subset closure R(k), or onto(k), makes the first test sufficient; the corresponding dual condition applies to N. The 2019 preprint theorem ALREADY assumes onto(k) and onto(k*) and is NOT contradicted; the false unconditional theorem is the 2020 journal version. Source files result/proof/verification/review/slogan/metadata/audit fully inspected, all six Git blob identities and complete tree matched. No numerical experiment replaces the operator proof.

value.rationale: The 2020 published theorem purports to replace full continuous K-dual reconstruction by two scalar norm identities. A transparent C² Parseval example falsifies both unconditional statements and proves exactly which reconstruction component is invisible, so it is a motivated correction with direct implications for selecting continuous K-duals. Although complex polarization and the onto special case were already known (indeed the 2019 preprint stated onto), the journal introduced a broader false theorem. Demonstrating its false positives, and the exact projected statement that remains valid, is an independently useful source-specific repair rather than an arbitrary tiny or mechanical parameter slice.
residual_risks: The correction is modest and source-specific, not a new general duality framework; its significance depends on the 2020 unqualified theorem being used as printed.
